name: Baile Funk
summary: Brazilian funk carioca's tamborzão skeleton — kick on 1 and 3, clap on 2 and 4, syncopated ghost hits pushed into the gaps — voiced across its named microstyles: airy beat bolha, the accelerated 150 BPM beat de faixa, São Paulo's minimal mandelão, and the dark bruxaria/automotivo wave. Atabaque and timbau rolls map onto tomLow/tomMid/congaLow/congaHigh, and tamborim rhythms map onto the tambourine role.

sounds.kick: 808-style kick, short and punchy, doubled with a sub for automotivo/faixa lanes; softer and sparser for beat bolha.
sounds.snare: Clap (the perc slot) carries the 2-and-4 backbeat almost everywhere; a real snare or rim substitutes in mandelão's clipped, minimalist voicing.
sounds.hats: Sparse, low-velocity closed hats or a continuous rolling shaker rather than a driving hat pattern; open hat used only as an occasional accent.
sounds.percussion: Atabaque/timbau layered onto tomLow, tomMid, congaHigh and congaLow for rolling syncopation; tamborim rhythms sit on the tambourine role; cowbell for bruxaria's bell-toll accents.
sounds.cymbals: Essentially unused — baile funk's low end and percussion carry the energy, not cymbal washes.

machines: Roland TR-808 — kick and clap foundation, the genre's core bass/clap source (owned)
Roland TR-727 — atabaque/timbau-style conga and tom hits for tamborzão percussion loops (owned)
Korg Electribe ER-1 / Elektron Machinedrum — synthesised percussion loops for bruxaria/automotivo textures (owned)
E-mu SP-1200 / Akai MPC60 — chopping and resampling atabaque/timbau breaks in the sample-based tradition (owned)
Sample packs of atabaque, timbau, tamborim and cuíca one-shots — the genre's actual percussion voice (get elsewhere)
references: MC Marcinho — early tamborzão-era funk carioca
Tati Quebra-Barraco — funk carioca vocal tradition
Rennan da Penha — Baile da Gaiola, funk 150 BPM / beat de faixa
Various Artists — funk bruxaria SoundCloud scene (2020s)
